Home / ADHD therapy

ADHD therapy for adults.

For adults who were told they were too much, not trying hard enough, or just anxious, and later found out it was ADHD. Or are starting to wonder.

Late diagnosis is common

A lot of adults, especially women and AFAB folks, get an ADHD diagnosis in their 30s or 40s, often after one of their kids is diagnosed. Before that, it gets called anxiety, depression or a personality flaw. Many people spent years masking: over-preparing, people-pleasing and running on stress to keep up.

What we work on

  • Making sense of a late diagnosis, including the grief that can come with it
  • Rejection sensitivity and emotional intensity
  • Shame from years of being called lazy or careless
  • How hormones, perimenopause and the menstrual cycle change symptoms
  • ADHD in relationships and parenting
  • The overlap with autism and with trauma

How therapy helps

Therapy here isn't about forcing your brain into a system built for someone else. It's about understanding how you work, dropping the shame, and building routines and boundaries that fit. Some of our therapists bring in IFS or EMDR when old hurts are part of the picture.

Read more first

Amy writes often about ADHD in women. Start with why ADHD in women gets missed or rejection sensitivity and ADHD.

Who to see

On the team

Amy Moreno, LPCADHD in women, later-in-life diagnosis. Telehealth.
Tiffany Sersen, MSWADHD, autism and burnout. Colorado Springs + telehealth.
Tatianna Saunders, LPCCNeurodivergent adults and creatives. Boulder + telehealth.
Emma Lewallen, MFTCADHD and autism in kids, teens and families. LoHi + telehealth.
Free 15 min consult

Common questions

Do I need a diagnosis to start?

No. Plenty of people start therapy because they suspect ADHD. If you want a formal evaluation, we can talk about where to get one.

Do you prescribe medication?

No. Our therapists are counselors, not prescribers. We're happy to work alongside your doctor or psychiatric provider.

Is online therapy okay for ADHD?

For many people it's easier. No commute, fewer missed appointments, and you can be somewhere comfortable.

Wherever you are in the process, we'll meet you there.

Home / EMDR

EMDR therapy.

A structured way to help your brain reprocess painful memories so they stop running the show. Without having to retell every detail.

What EMDR is

Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) helps the brain reprocess painful or overwhelming memories so they no longer feel as triggering. It can reduce symptoms of PTSD, anxiety and depression, and help you feel calmer and more in control.

What a session looks like

Early sessions are about history, safety and skills for calming your nervous system. When you're ready, your therapist guides you to briefly hold a memory in mind while using bilateral stimulation, such as eye movements or tapping. You stay in charge of the pace, and you don't have to describe everything out loud.

Who it tends to help

  • PTSD and complex trauma
  • Anxiety and panic
  • Grief and loss
  • Childhood experiences that still shape how you react today
  • Medical or birth trauma

EMDR with IFS

Some of our therapists combine EMDR with Internal Family Systems. EMDR lowers the charge on a memory, and IFS supports the parts of you that have been carrying it. Read about IFS and Brainspotting, or Amy's post on the magic of EMDR.

Who to see

On the team

Amy Moreno, LPCEMDR Certified, IFS-informed EMDR. Telehealth.
Tiffany Sersen, MSWSomatic EMDR. Colorado Springs + telehealth.
Kelsey Loupy, PhD, LPCCEMDR trained. Boulder + telehealth.
Free 15 min consult

Common questions

Does EMDR work over video?

Yes. Many clients find online EMDR just as effective as in-person sessions, with the bonus of being at home afterward.

How many sessions does it take?

It depends on what you're working on. A single recent event can move quickly. Complex or childhood trauma takes longer. Your therapist will talk this through with you.

Will I have to relive the trauma?

No. EMDR doesn't require going through every detail. You stay in the present while the memory is processed.

Home / IFS and Brainspotting

IFS and Brainspotting.

For people who want to go underneath the story. Parts work and brain-body approaches, for when talking about it hasn't been enough.

Internal Family Systems

IFS starts from the idea that we all have different parts. Some carry pain, some protect us, some try to keep everything under control. Instead of fighting the critical or anxious parts, IFS helps you get curious about them and find out what they're protecting. That opens up room for healing and for your own steady sense of Self.

Brainspotting

Brainspotting is a body-based trauma therapy. By focusing on specific eye positions linked to emotional and physical experience, it helps you reach and process feelings and memories that sit below conscious awareness. People often find it useful when words feel like too little, or when years of talk therapy haven't reached the root.

What they help with

  • Complex trauma and C-PTSD
  • Anxiety, panic and burnout
  • Harsh self-criticism and perfectionism
  • Relationship patterns and attachment wounds
  • Feeling stuck after other therapy

Choosing an approach

You don't have to know which one you want. On your consult call we'll talk about your goals and match you with a therapist. These approaches also pair well with EMDR.

Home / Affirming care

Neurodivergent and LGBTQIA+ affirming care.

Queer, trans, nonbinary, autistic, ADHD, highly sensitive, ethically non-monogamous. You don't have to explain or translate yourself here.

What affirming means here

It means you won't spend your sessions educating your therapist. Your identity, your relationships and the way your brain works aren't the problem to be fixed. We focus on what you came in for, whether that's trauma, anxiety, burnout, family stuff or something else entirely.

Who we see

  • LGBTQIA+ adults, teens and couples
  • Trans and nonbinary clients
  • People in open, polyamorous and other ENM relationships
  • Autistic and ADHD adults, including late-diagnosed folks
  • Highly sensitive people and creatives
  • Deaf and hard of hearing clients (ASL with Tiffany)

Years of masking

Many of our clients have spent years shape-shifting to be accepted, at home, at work, even in past therapy. That takes a toll. We go at your pace, and we work with the trauma that often sits underneath.

Home / Perinatal and postpartum

Perinatal and postpartum therapy.

Trying to conceive, pregnant, grieving a loss, or in the blur of the first year. Support for the parts nobody warned you about.

What we help with

  • Anxiety and intrusive thoughts during pregnancy or after birth
  • Postpartum depression and rage
  • Fertility struggles and pregnancy loss
  • Birth trauma
  • Identity shifts and the strain on your relationship
  • Going back to work, or not

You're not failing

The perinatal years can bring up old anxiety, old trauma and a lot of pressure to be grateful all the time. Therapy is a place to say the hard stuff out loud without being judged for it.

How it works

Sessions can be in person in Golden or LoHi, or online from your couch with a baby asleep on you. Our therapists use IFS, nature-based approaches and other trauma-informed methods.

Home / Privacy policy

Privacy policy.

Written in plain language. If anything here is unclear, ask.

What this covers

This policy covers rebuildingtogethercounseling.com. Your health information as a client is covered separately by the Notice of Privacy Practices you receive at intake, which follows HIPAA.

What the site collects

When you use a contact form or book a consult, we collect what you enter, such as your name, email, phone number and message. We use it only to respond to you and set up care.

The site is hosted on Squarespace, which keeps standard logs and may set cookies to run the site and measure traffic. Scheduling runs through Acuity. You can block cookies in your browser and the site will still work.

Email is not fully secure

Please keep detailed health information out of forms and email. Save it for your consult call or first session.

What we don't do

We never sell or rent your information, and we won't add you to a mailing list without asking.

Your choices

You can ask us to delete a form message that hasn't become part of a client record. Email amy@rebuildingtogethercounseling.com or call 303-351-1307.

Changes

If this policy changes, we'll update the date below.

Terms of use.

By using this website, you agree to these terms. If you don't agree, please don't use the site.

Information, not treatment

Everything on this site is general information. It isn't medical or mental health advice and doesn't replace an evaluation by a qualified professional. Using the site, a form or email doesn't create a therapist-client relationship. That begins after intake and signed informed consent.

In a crisis

This website, our email and our phones are not monitored around the clock and are not for emergencies. If you are in crisis, call or text 988, call 911, or go to the nearest emergency room.

Telehealth eligibility

Our therapists are licensed in Colorado. For telehealth sessions you need to be physically in Colorado at the time of each session, unless your therapist confirms otherwise.

Fees

Fees and insurance listed on this site can change. Your cost will be confirmed before your first session.
